verse.text: For if we have been united with him in a death like his, we will certainly also be united with him in a resurrection like his.

reflection.scripture: For if we have been united with him in a death like his, we will certainly also be united with him in a resurrection like his.
reflection.observation: Paul draws a powerful parallel between Christ's death and resurrection and our own spiritual journey. Just as Jesus physically died and rose again, we who have placed our faith in Him have been spiritually united with Him in death to sin — and that same union guarantees our future resurrection. This isn't wishful thinking; it's a certainty rooted in our identification with Christ. The word 'certainly' (or 'indeed' in some translations) underscores the absolute confidence we can have.
reflection.application: Today, I want to live in the reality of my union with Christ. If I am truly dead to sin, I don't need to let old patterns, anxieties, or temptations dictate my choices. I can walk in the power of resurrection life right now — not perfectly, but progressively. When I face a moment of weakness today, I'll pause and remind myself: I am united with Christ. His resurrection power is at work in me.
reflection.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You that my identity is secure in You. I am united with You in Your death and resurrection. Help me live today in the power of that truth. When sin tempts me, remind me that I am dead to it. When discouragement comes, remind me that Your resurrection life is mine. Fill me with hope and holy courage to walk in newness of life. In Your mighty name, Amen.
